headline: Highest risk is medium: shared write-capable marketing agent can inject or cascade content into a read-only documentation agent, but B’s no-write/no-network profile limits blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can write files and uses shared-context skill patterns, so malicious or malformed marketing content could be placed where Agent B later reads it as reference. Agent B has no filesystem read surface, clipboard, or MCP, so the direct bridge is weak; uncertainty about the exact orchestration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Agent B is later connected to a shared workspace or file reader, injected instructions can propagate.
IF Agent A writes attacker-controlled content into a shared context file, B may ingest it as guidance.
mitigations: Restrict Agent A to a dedicated output directory.
Disable shared-context file handoff between the agents.
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-authored content.
Use content markers that B treats as untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read and write files and has allowlisted egress, but Agent B has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no declared data classes. The pair does not show a default path for sensitive data to leave B; the main risk is limited to unusual operator wiring or shared files not documented here.
conditions: IF an operator places sensitive files into a shared directory that Agent A can read, A may transmit them over allowlisted egress.
IF Agent B is given sensitive inputs outside its documented surfaces, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any directory Agent A can read.
Limit Agent A egress allowlist to non-sensitive destinations.
Do not pass secrets or regulated data into either agent.
Review file paths before launching Agent A.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Agent B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only plausible conflict is if an external orchestrator gives both access to the same mutable workspace, which is not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted onto the same writable directory by an external orchestrator, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF Agent A is extended with git access outside this profile, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Prevent concurrent launches against the same repo.
Keep Agent B read-only as documented.
Avoid letting Agent A spawn subprocesses in shared paths.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or workspace leasing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A’s output can become downstream content for Agent B because the sandboxing notes say skills build on shared context. Agent B is documentation-only and may render or reuse A’s text without verification, so errors can cascade into incorrect marketing or reference material. The blast radius is bounded by content quality, not system control.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A’s generated text as authoritative reference, errors can propagate.
IF A produces unsupported claims and B republishes them, downstream content becomes incorrect.
mitigations: Require B to cite source material explicitly.
Add a verification checklist before publication.
Mark A-generated text as draft only.
Have a human review factual claims before reuse.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware content validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Agent A touches marketing content and product marketing context, while Agent B touches no declared data classes and has no network or file surfaces. With no PHI, EU PII, retention, or residency signals in either profile, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into Agent A’s marketing context, compliance review is required.
IF Agent B is later assigned retention or residency-sensitive data, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data-class boundaries before use.
Review retention settings for any shared storage.
Confirm no PHI or EU PII enters the workflow.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
